t: A Modern Guide to Collecting Miles Davis | Tracking Angle
s: 6-eye copies of the earlier albums are either beat up or incredibly expensive, originals of the “Second Great Quintet” albums don’t have the highest sonic reputation, and buying a vintage Get Up With It seems dubious considering its half-hour sides. The three albums I’ve plucked for comparison are 1958’s Milestones, 1968’s Miles In The Sky, and 1970’s Jack Johnson. And if digital sources are a problem, you’re out of luck. Over several Record Store Day events in 2012-2013, Sony/Legacy reissued Miles Davis’ early Columbia albums in mono, mostly cut by Kevin Gray from hi-res digital files.
